opening.quote: Good morning, Tidewell Home, my name is Lotte. How can I help?
opening.comment: You gave your name and the company name in your first turn, which meets the opening standard.

verification.quote: Name and order number or postcode.
verification.comment: You asked for the details before discussing the order, but you accepted the caller's full name and order number, so this meets the standard.

understanding.quote: Okay, Siobhan. Chair, €95.00, delivered 41 days ago. You want to return it because you don't like it?
understanding.comment: You captured the issue accurately and did not ask for information the caller had already given.

resolution_accuracy.quote: Our return window is 30 days from delivery, so I can't accept a return now.
resolution_accuracy.comment: The 30-day return window and the refusal are correct, though you could have explained the warranty options for a faulty electrical item, and you did not check whether the chair is faulty.

process_compliance.quote: Those are the rules. I'll email you this information today. Anything else?
process_compliance.comment: No policy step was triggered here, since the caller did not report a damaged or faulty item and no hold or chargeback occurred, so this is compliant.

communication.comment: When the caller said she was disappointed and hated the chair, you did not acknowledge her frustration, and 'Those are the rules' came across as curt; please acknowledge the feeling before explaining the policy.

closing.quote: Thank you for calling Tidewell. Goodbye.
closing.comment: You closed politely and asked if there was anything else, but you did not clearly confirm what happens next beyond saying you would send an email, so the closing is only partly complete.
